part.text: The file has complete annual coverage for 2013–2025 and includes motorist deaths and crash counts, but no miles-driven exposure. I’ll chart three supportable alternatives: annual deaths, deaths per reported crash, and the share of crashes with a motorist death; none can establish per-mile risk.

input.command:
python -c $'import os, json
import duckdb, pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

os.makedirs("out", exist_ok=True)
con = duckdb.connect()
p = "data/crashes.parquet"
df = con.execute(f"""
    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
           count(*) AS crash_count,
           sum(number_of_motorist_killed) AS motorist_deaths,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_motorist_killed > 0) AS fatal_motorist_crashes,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE crash_date IS NULL) AS null_date_rows,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_motorist_killed IS NULL) AS null_death_rows,
           min(crash_date) AS first_date, max(crash_date) AS last_date
    FROM read_parquet('{p}')
    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01' AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
""").df()
df["deaths_per_1000_crashes"] = df.motorist_deaths / df.crash_count * 1000
df["fatal_motorist_crash_pct"] = df.fatal_motorist_crashes / df.crash_count * 100

# Option 1: absolute annual burden
v1 = df[["year", "motorist_deaths"]].copy()
v1.to_csv("out/values_1.csv", index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ax.bar(v1.year, v1.motorist_deaths, color="#3973ac")
ax.set(title="Motorists killed in NYC crashes, 2013–2025", xlabel="Crash year", ylabel="Motorists killed (people)")
ax.set_xticks(v1.year); ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45); ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=.25)
fig.text(.5, .01, "Counts do not adjust for miles driven", ha="center", color="#555")
fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, .05, 1, 1)); fig.savefig("out/option_1.png", dpi=160); plt.close(fig)

# Option 2: fatalities normalized by reported crash count
v2 = df[["year", "motorist_deaths", "crash_count", "deaths_per_1000_crashes"]].copy()
v2.to_csv("out/values_2.csv", index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ax.plot(v2.year, v2.deaths_per_1000_crashes, marker="o", color="#c04b37")
ax.set(title="Motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crashes, 2013–2025", xlabel="Crash year", ylabel="Motorist deaths per 1,000 crash records")
ax.set_xticks(v2.year); ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45); ax.grid(alpha=.25)
fig.text(.5, .01, "Crash-normalized measure; not a per-mile risk rate", ha="center", color="#555")
fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, .05, 1, 1)); fig.savefig("out/option_2.png", dpi=160); plt.close(fig)

# Option 3: incidence of a crash with at least one motorist killed
v3 = df[["year", "fatal_motorist_crashes", "crash_count", "fatal_motorist_crash_pct"]].copy()
v3.to_csv("out/values_3.csv", index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ax.plot(v3.year, v3.fatal_motorist_crash_pct, marker="o", color="#49875a")
ax.set(title="Share of NYC crash records with a motorist killed, 2013–2025", xlabel="Crash year", ylabel="Crashes with ≥1 motorist killed (%)")
ax.set_xticks(v3.year); ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45); ax.grid(alpha=.25)
fig.text(.5, .01, "Crash-level incidence; not a per-mile risk rate", ha="center", color="#555")
fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, .05, 1, 1)); fig.savefig("out/option_3.png", dpi=160); plt.close(fig)

# machine-readable coverage/null audit for constructing interpretations
df.to_csv("/tmp/crash_yearly_audit.csv", index=False)
print(df.to_string(index=False))'
